## Implemented on the client (logic proven in Node; platform bindings named)

Field runtime: contracts, envelope crypto, durable outbox, sync engine,
browser fallback. Carried communication packages: fetched, hash-verified on
this side, written to the encrypted vault, read back before being acknowledged,
read again on every open, and refused rather than shown when they no longer
match what was stored — proven in Node against the runtime contracts, with the
native vault still a stub. Internal portal: shell, switcher, My Day, exceptions,
inbox, timeline, search, sync indicator, quick capture, view-models.
Training Academy at `/training-academy`: course catalog, My Training, current-version lesson completion, locked/unlocked final assessment, results, certificate/qualification portfolio, and self-signing of pending regulated certificates.
Customer portal at `/customer`: invitation acceptance, job board,
pre-clearance, signing screen, chain of custody, adjustments, line disputes,
approval queue, timeline, alerts and preferences, documents with download,
notices, daily report. Vendor and facility portal at `/vendor` and
`/facility`: statements and submissions. First-run setup wizard in the
office portals: company, services, guardrails, rates with approval,
readiness — every step the server's answer.

## Not implemented — and not claimed

Native shell (Capacitor), encrypted SQLite, hardware keystore, native file
vault, camera, GPS, biometric signing, local notifications. Browser/mobile
end-to-end tests. LoadSense authenticated gateway ingestion/native BLE service and hardware deployment (the recovered protocol, calibration/stability/material-movement engines and persistence model are present; the production machine-authenticated device edge is not yet wired). Routing services (a native graph built from imported Alberta road data routes within built areas; no provincial routing source — P0 outside them; PostGIS/Valhalla/Martin/MapLibre not deployed; ATS v4.1 importable per township and imported where a person has run it — coordinates are verified one at a time with evidence). Radio and coverage data as imports (the ISED, BC and CRTC adapters are not written — channels are seeded or recorded by hand, road assignments are recorded or confirmed from a field observation, and coverage is whatever somebody has recorded; no cellular or spectrum layer has been ingested). Fluids as measured inventory (parts ledger only). Contracts and MSAs as
records; WBS below cost code; earned-value schedules. AI extraction of rate sheets from
uploaded documents (a proposal path exists; the document reader that fills
it does not); formula pricing is recorded, not evaluated. inbound
vendor bills and facility tickets by machine (portal only). GPS on the
board and route-derived segments (P0). Email/SMS delivery of customer alerts
(queued in-app only). Video clips in the vault (pointers and hashes only); posted speed limits
from a verified source (feed-supplied, marked unverified). Payroll final-pay computation on offboarding (proposed only). Package bundles as archives (manifest and cover only).

## Blocked on things only a person can do

**P9** — no regulatory, tax or rate rule is verified; every determination on
the seeds is UNKNOWN and the loading paths are controller-only.
**AER ST37 / ST102 / Alberta 511** — inspection-only pending written permission.
**P9 — hours of service.** Every seeded HOS profile and every figure in it is
unverified, so every determination reads UNKNOWN and the clocks show without a
compliance answer. BC oil-well service and the three territorial schedules are
seeded deliberately empty. Verifying is controller/management only, one figure
at a time against its clause.
**A package is only as current as the last rebuild.** LeaseOS detects staleness
and names it; nothing rebuilds automatically, and no notification reaches a
driver who has already left.
**No communication policy is seeded.** Until two people approve one, dispatch
warns about communications and stops nothing — which is the right default and
not a working configuration.
The order carries the typed act it demands alongside the issuing authority's own
words, never inferred by parsing them, so a satisfied repair verification cannot
lift an order that requires a reinspection. One test walks a roadside prohibition from a driver's scan to a cleared
dispatch through the product itself — the scan, the confirmation, the finding
and the release all through the API, with real rows for the event, order,
defect, work order, outbox entry and notifications. Every step runs through the API, including the
shop's own advance and release of the work order, which had no procedure until
now — the technician on a release is the authenticated caller and never anything
the request body said, because a release attributed to somebody who did not give
it is worse than no release at all. A work order moves forward only. A second, older test walks the
enforcement core against the database — offline
capture, local block, confirmation, atomic commit, viewed-not-acknowledged,
escalation, acknowledgement, repair, refusal, reinspection, explicit release,
latch lift — asserting the chronology rather than the final state, because a
final state of ready can be reached by a chain that was unsafe at every
intermediate step. Its edges are still in memory: the outbox is a callback, the
notifications are constructed, and the repair is a literal, so it is an
integration test of the core and not yet the production path. A tablet holding a confirmed out-of-service capture prohibits the subject before
the server has heard of it, reports that claim to the office as an observation
that creates no prohibition of its own, and asks the server what it may lift.
Only a released or rescinded order answers lift; an order still active, or one
the server has never heard of, answers hold — so a device that cannot be told to
lift keeps blocking. Synchronizing does not lift that latch — it adds
server identity and nothing else. Only the authoritative released or rescinded
state of that same order lifts it. What the device claimed about its own
authorization at the moment of capture is history: it survives synchronization
unchanged, whether the upload succeeded or failed. Who may record which kind of
release finding, and whether the releaser must differ from the repairer, is a
versioned policy whose organization the caller cannot choose — the tenant comes
from server-owned context and a branch-confined grant cannot write policy for
another branch — proposed by one person and approved by a different one,
effective-dated and superseded rather than overwritten, which an auditor can
read as it stood on the day and whose ref and version the released order itself
carries so nothing has to be reconstructed. Approval is serialized per scope and refuses to leave two
approved policies overlapping at one scope, because that would manufacture the
ambiguity the release selector then refuses — and the first anyone would learn
of it is a truck nobody can release. Which policy governs is decided by the scope
snapshotted on the order when the stop was confirmed, most specific first —
terminal, then branch, then company, within that tenant only — so another
branch's policy cannot govern this one and transferring the asset afterwards
cannot move the rules; two approved policies overlapping at the same specificity
block the release rather than being resolved by guessing at version — and no
policy can make a repair verification satisfy an order that demands a
reinspection. A real domain-event row is written inside the same transaction as the order, so
a prohibition cannot be saved while the office is never told and no alert exists
for a transaction that rolled back; severity follows the facts rather than a
caller's opinion. A separate consumer claims those rows and writes one
notification per role at the first escalation level, keyed by event and
recipient so that running it twice — or crashing between writing the
notifications and marking the event claimed — tells nobody twice. A routine
confirmation is claimed and wakes nobody: a record, not an alarm. Escalation reads the delivery states the workflow notifications table
already records: viewing is not acceptance and does not stop the ladder, a push
that failed leaves the in-app notification outstanding and the ladder still
climbs, the clock runs from when the stop happened rather than when a message
was sent, any one acknowledgement stops it, and roles named in the company's
critical-response policy cannot opt out of that class while they hold the role.
A violation that requires work reaches the shop queue in the same transaction as
the prohibition it came from: the defect and work order are created and linked
back to the violation, so a grounded truck never sits with nothing in the queue
explaining why, and the release path has real repair records to read rather than
a sentence in a return value. A prohibition is critical work; a required repair
needs inspecting; a citation that required neither raises nothing. The enforcement surface is reachable from a client and supplies its own facts:
the organization, the confirming person, the finding's author and role, and —
above all — the repairs come from server-owned records, so a caller cannot
assert what was fixed and free a prohibited truck. A scan is recorded as a
proposal that decides nothing, a finding is refused unless the approved policy
for that order's own scope permits that role to record it, and a release names
only the order. A confirmed stop commits as one transaction — event, violations, citations and
orders together or not at all — keyed by what the act is rather than when it
ran, so a driver tapping confirm twice on a bad connection produces one set of
orders and not three. An out-of-service marking whose scope the document does
not state writes no order and says it needs confirming with the inspector,
because guessing either grounds a truck that was never prohibited or frees one
that was. A release finding is its own record with its own author and role, kept
whether it says satisfied, not satisfied or unknown; the latest is the answer
and the earlier ones are history; and an order becomes released only because
somebody called release, never because a repair finished. An active out-of-service order reaches the dispatch gate and is not overridable
by anyone in this company — a manager may override a company rule, and an
inspector's order is not one. A mechanic establishes that a truck is
mechanically sound and nothing more; before this the composer had no idea
enforcement existed and a release could report a prohibited unit available. An
out-of-service capture shares the top outbox tier with HOS, so a prohibition
never queues behind photographs. An enforcement stop is read as six independent consequences rather than one
flag: a citation with no out-of-service marking stops nothing, an out-of-service
marking with no citation still prohibits, and an order is scoped to the driver,
vehicle, trailer, cargo or carrier so a prohibited driver on a clear truck is
reported as replaceable. An inspection whose result nobody established denies
authorization rather than reading as a pass. A completed, tested, evidenced
repair reaches repair-complete-pending-release and no further — the order's own
release condition is a separate finding; who may record which kind of finding,
and whether the releaser must differ from the repairer, is determined by the
applicable release policy and can never weaken the issuing authority's own
condition. No path lifts a prohibition without that finding. Scanned documents are proposals requiring
confirmation, inspection report numbers and citation numbers are separate
fields, and LeaseOS stores its own violation identifiers with a citation of the
official source and no field for the licensed criteria text.

A dashboard tile that cannot say where its number came from does not render the
number — the failure belongs on the screen rather than behind a plausible
figure. A stale value renders as unavailable rather than as a number with a
small grey timestamp, because a fuel level from a truck that lost signal at
06:00 otherwise looks exactly like one from thirty seconds ago and somebody
plans a route on it. A compliance tile never rounds up: three of four checks
passing with the fourth unevaluated reads unknown, not green. A person may
rearrange their dashboard and may not hide a safety or compliance tile, since
hiding an alert does not resolve what it is alerting about.

A field device is the source of truth for what it observed and never the source
of authority for what that observation permits. A driver with no signal records
a defect, captures a signature, completes a tailgate and dictates a ticket —
those are facts and they survive to sync — while a server-authoritative
capability is never executed locally, only prepared and queued, or declared
unavailable in plain words rather than appearing to work and failing hours later
at the edge of coverage. The offline class is declared with the capability and
bound to the gateway's risk levels, so a server decision cannot be labelled a
local read, and a test names the exact mismatch if one side moves alone. What
syncs is evidence: the device's own assessment travels as a claim with its
basis, because "the local model thought the route was legal" and "the route is
legal" read identically to a database column and entirely differently to a
regulator. A cached answer with no capture time is unknown rather than current.

Nothing becomes model-readable because somebody built an object that looks
right. An admitted block can only be produced by the admission module — the type
carries a symbol no other file can name, so a hand-built block is a compile
error rather than a runtime hope, and there is deliberately no generic admit()
taking kind, tenant and text, since whoever can pass those three can manufacture
authority. A resolver states how it knows which organization owns a row, and a
row owned only by the single-tenant assumption becomes refusable the moment a
second organization exists: AI context is not where unfinished multi-tenancy
gets completed. A reference belonging to another organization answers exactly as
a made-up one does. Fields are projected by name rather than trimmed after
loading, so a column added next year is absent by default instead of opted in.

An engine nothing imports is a rule waiting to be written twice, so that is now
a gate check rather than something a reader notices. Reachability is measured through the import graph rather than by direct
importers: two earlier versions of the check were each wrong in one direction,
one letting a pair of engines cite each other and both look wired, the other
calling a router's genuine one-hop dependency unreached. Forty engines are
unreachable from any application path; each is named with the reason it is not wired,
and the gate fails both if an undeclared one appears and if a declared one is
wired without being removed from the list. The check found a live duplication
immediately: the open-shift eligibility engine exists and the router that
answers eligibility decides inline instead.

Whether a qualification counts is decided in one place. The canonical engine was
written and then imported by nothing, while four routers each decided the same
question inline — four correct-looking implementations of one rule, which is how
they stop agreeing. They now share an adapter, and the verdict carries a
structured code rather than prose the caller matches on: the previous version
classified by searching the reason text and silently reclassified every
unverified ticket the moment that wording improved.

A document on file is not a document in force. An upload is unverified, an OCR
extraction is still nobody's assertion, and only a person checking the page
against the dates puts a version in force — which matters because the folder
looks full either way. A newly uploaded version does not displace a verified
one: the 2027 certificate uploaded in November takes effect when somebody
confirms it, and the previous version is superseded rather than deleted. An
expiry blocks the capabilities that depend on that document and no others, so an
expired dangerous-goods endorsement stops dangerous-goods work and leaves water
hauling alone — grounding the person entirely produces overrides until the
overrides mean nothing. Unverified and missing block exactly as expired does,
being the same operational fact in different clothes.

Attachments are persisted as references and reachable. One resolver per object
kind, no default and no permission built by joining strings — an unresolvable
kind is refused rather than guessed at. Three kinds ship (job, defect, unit)
because those are the ones this schema can actually resolve; invoices exist and
are deliberately not shipped, since a financial record wants a real row-level
rule rather than an existence check wearing one. None of those tables carries an
organization column, so their scope is the deployment's single tenant and the
registry says so rather than implying otherwise. Client channels take no
attachments at all: there is no client-side authorization path for an internal
record, so nothing is attachable there rather than everything. Every attachment
is resolved before a single row is written and the whole post rolls back if one
is refused. A body revision is not an attachment revision, and withdrawal is not
erasure.

An attachment is a reference and never a copy, so a message cannot become a way
around a record's permissions. The sender must be able to open what they attach,
and every reader is checked against the object rather than against the
conversation — the sender's authority is the sender's and does not travel with
the message. A reader without access sees a stub naming what is attached and
nothing more, because hiding it entirely would make "see attached" read as a
broken message while showing it would be the leak. Payroll documents, employee
records and client contracts are never attachable at all, even by somebody who
can open them, since attaching means showing it to the room. Access is evaluated
at read time, so a permission revoked yesterday closes the attachment today. An
object from another organization is refused in the same words as one that does
not exist.

Every path into a crew message applies the same boundary, because it lives in
channel admission rather than in whichever resolver remembered it — history and
the acknowledgement roster were reachable with a message reference alone until
that moved. A message reference is a locator and never a capability: refusals on
those paths all read the same, so holding one distinguishes nothing, and a
cross-tenant message no longer answers differently from a missing one. Current
membership is temporal — a joining date tomorrow is not membership today, and
such a person is neither admitted nor mistaken for a historical member. Reading
what you were sent survives leaving the crew; changing it does not, and a
read-only crew stops accepting revisions rather than continuing to append to a
closed record. A post and its audience commit in one transaction under one
acceptance timestamp, and a crew larger than the audience this board records is
refused rather than silently redefined as its first five hundred members.

A channel carrying a crew is reachable only through actual membership: being an
internal user is not being in this crew, and the generic rule that admitted any
employee to any non-private channel was wrong the moment a channel carried one.
The audience is snapshotted into receipts when the server accepts a post, so
history is what was really recorded rather than something re-derived later from
mutable membership — a person who joined today does not inherit yesterday's
conversation, and one who left keeps what they were sent. The device clock never
widens access: a message backdated to before somebody left the crew does not
reach them, because a backdated clock would otherwise be an authorization
primitive. Callers cannot name crew recipients at all. A channel is a client
channel or a crew channel, never both.

Being added to a crew grants crew things and nothing else: the permissions are
enumerated and every one is namespaced to the crew, so membership assembled
automatically by dispatch cannot quietly become the privileged path. Ending an
assignment sets a leaving date rather than removing the row — deleting it would
make somebody's messages authored by a person who was never there — and a former
member reads what was posted while they were present, not a line before or
after. A job crew stops accepting when its job closes and keeps everything,
because a record that can still be appended to after an invoice is disputed is
not a record. A mention reaches its own scope, since one that reaches everybody
is how a crew learns to ignore the one that mattered.

A receipt advances forward only and on evidence: a queued message reads "Queued
— no signal", an accepted one reads "Sent", and nothing reads "Delivered" until
it reached the recipient's device — a tick that means delivered when it does not
is the lie a sender acts on, and for a stop-work order it is the one that gets
somebody hurt. Only the recipient can acknowledge their own receipt. In a
roll-call nobody is counted safe by default: those who read the notice and said
nothing are listed apart from those it never reached, since one needs a radio
call and the other needs somebody to drive out, and the call stays unsettled
while anybody needs assistance. A message is edited by appending a revision and
withdrawn without erasure — what recipients acted on stays readable.

The board is reachable. Access is decided on the channel before any message is
read, so a client reaches their own channel and no internal one, and a client
channel that names no client is refused at creation because that reference is
what decides who may open it. Both clocks are stored: a message recorded on a
tablet three hours before it reached the server keeps each time, and the sender
reads "Sent" rather than "Delivered" while the server holds it. Acknowledgement
is derived from priority, so an urgent bulletin cannot be posted as ignorable,
and opening one is counted apart from accepting it. Receipts do not move
backwards. There is one receipt vocabulary. The eight-state lifecycle is authoritative and
the board's acknowledgement summary reads evidence timestamps rather than state
names — a receipt that reached resolved was acknowledged on the way, and
translating the name back to discover that would invent a lossy mapping to
answer what the timestamps already answer. The original message body is stored
once and turned into revision 1 by a single constructor, because writing that
construction out per resolver is the two-writable-originals hazard in a
different coat.

A message on the board can become a defect, a hazard or an incident, and becomes
none of them by itself: it produces a suggestion carrying the driver's own words
verbatim, and a person completes the record — text is an observation, and a
compliance record created silently from it is a finding nobody made. Client
channels are separated rather than filtered, because a per-message filter is one
somebody eventually forgets. Reading a bulletin is not acknowledging it, and
those who read without acknowledging are counted apart from those it never
reached. An offline message keeps both clocks: the device's is when it happened,
the server's when it arrived, and the first is never overwritten.

A request supplies a payload; the server hashes it. A caller-supplied hash would
only prove that the string shown at approval matched the string shown at
execution, not that the thing approved is the thing done — and keys are sorted
before hashing so a re-send serialised differently still matches its approval.
Origin, the compliance verdict and the target's current revision are server-owned
and accepted from nobody: company policy outranks an authorized user on the
instruction ladder, a caller supplying a compliance result is a caller deciding
compliance, and the stale check exists precisely to catch an edit the caller has
not seen. The server currently establishes no compliance verdict and no current
revision, so those two gateway paths are unreachable from the API and three
router tests are skipped saying so rather than passing against facts the request
invented.

Agent runs, steps, gateway decisions and approvals are persisted, and every
verdict is recorded including the refusals — a log of only what succeeded cannot
answer "why didn't it", which is the question people actually ask about an
agent. An action requested through the runtime is the agent acting whoever asked
for it: the caller does not supply the actor type, because the check that
refuses an agent the never-autonomous capabilities turns on exactly that field
and letting the request choose it would make the refusal opt-out. Nor may a
caller claim an authority above an authorized user, since accepting "system"
over the wire would launder external content into the top of the instruction
ladder.

A model context is assembled for one organization and refuses rather than
filters: loading two companies' data and instructing the model to discuss one is
a request, not isolation, and the one unusual question is all that stands
between the data and the answer. A block naming no organization is refused too,
because the assumption is always that it belongs and the one time it does not is
the incident. Content cannot instruct whatever it says — a document's authority
comes from where it came from, never from anything it claims about itself — so
text reading "ignore all previous instructions" is carried intact as data rather
than stripped, since stripping is lossy and the phrasings are not enumerable.
Instruction-shaped text is flagged for a person and has no effect on what the
block may do, which is already nothing.

This document was generated by a script whose heredoc was unquoted, so bash read
the prose as shell syntax. Every backticked term was executed as a command and
replaced by its output — for a word like `prohibited`, nothing — so terms
vanished from the page while the gate reported it current, because a failed
substitution is not a failed script. The body is now a quoted heredoc and bash
interprets none of it; the thirteen values that genuinely vary are named
placeholders substituted afterwards, and an unresolved one fails generation
rather than printing itself on the page. The test requires a clean exit and
empty output, and reads the rendered document rather than trusting the source
that produced it.

A permission a resolver declares is now actually checked. Admission recorded it
in the receipt and admitted the block regardless, so a resolver could say it
required payroll access and a dispatcher would read the record anyway — with the
receipt afterwards looking like evidence of a check that never ran, which is
worse than no receipt at all. It refuses in the same words as absent and
foreign, so holding a real reference to something you may not read teaches
nothing. The passage resolver names a permission this system defines rather than
one that named nothing, and whether the deployment serves more than one
organization is derived from how the caller's scope was established rather than
frozen at false, where the refusal it guards could never have fired.

Asking carries two clocks: the caller chooses which day's documents to answer
from, and the server stamps when the question was asked. One field did both, so
a caller could date a row in the table whose whole purpose is showing what was
asked and when.

The grade is computed on real questions alone. Averaging across every probe let
a single real question unlock a figure dominated by questions written from the
passages — twenty-five easy self-vocabulary hits and one real-world miss came
out near ninety per cent and called the retriever adequate.

A recall figure is a figure about one corpus, one retriever and one depth, and
any of the three moving makes it about something else. The corpus hash was only
the first of those: when lexical retrieval becomes hybrid the documents can stay
byte-for-byte identical while the implementation changes completely, and the old
measurement would have gone on certifying the new one. Depth belongs to identity
for the same reason — recall at twenty is a true number about a product showing
twenty, and an answer showing eight cannot borrow it. Measuring records a
measurement, so it is a mutation; it was a query, which is the mistake corrected
in the ask path one change earlier and not then looked for anywhere else. One
recorded ask yields one labelled question however many times a curator reviews
it, because five reviews are not five people asking.

Labelling has a screen, and the browse it offers is deliberately not the
retriever under test: a curator must be able to find a passage retrieval missed,
which is the case worth labelling, and a search built on the thing being
measured could only ever surface what already surfaced. It is a plain substring
scan — slower, dumber, and the only kind that can show somebody what their
retriever cannot see. Passages the assistant cited are marked as such and left
unticked, because a curator who simply confirms them has recorded that retrieval
agreed with itself, and the measurement would then be worthless in the
flattering direction. The question cannot be edited on the screen; rewording it
would make it a question nobody asked.

A real question is proved rather than claimed. The origin field arrived from the
request, so a curator could type a question while reading the passage, label it
as how people actually ask, and have the grade treat it as evidence of exactly
the thing it was not — the same shape as a caller asserting its own authority,
sitting inside the instrument meant to decide whether to buy a semantic
retriever. A real-question probe is now built from a recorded ask: the server
copies the words somebody actually typed and records which ask they came from,
and the authored path can no longer say otherwise. What labelling deliberately
does not do is adopt the passages the assistant returned — a curator names the
ones that should answer, which may include passages retrieval never surfaced,
and that gap is the entire measurement. Accepting the retrieved set would let
the retriever mark its own homework and then be graded on it.

The retrieval quality an answer reports is the one that was measured. It was
graded from an empty list, so the screen said "unmeasured" for ever — counting
probes beside a figure that ignored them, which is worse than showing no count
at all. A measurement now carries a hash of everything retrieval and grounding
consult, because the passage count and the newest-created date were description
rather than identity: superseding a passage changes what an answer may cite
while leaving both numbers exactly where they were. When the documents have
changed since a measurement, the answer says that figure describes a different
corpus rather than quietly reusing it.

Asking the documents has a screen, and asking is a mutation because it is
recorded: written as a query, a page refetching on window focus would have filed
a second question nobody asked, and a log padded with phantom asks is not
evidence of anything. The screen quotes passages rather than summarising them,
cites document, section, page and revision, and treats "nothing in the loaded
documents answers this" as the answer rather than an empty result — the
alternative being the helpful-sounding paragraph this whole path exists to
avoid. The retrieval caveat sits above the answer rather than below it, because
a reader who sees three citations assumes they are the three best unless told
otherwise, and putting that in grey at the bottom would be disclosure in name
only.

The route preview computes with a query and persists nothing, because a record
saying a plan was made for this trip is a claim about the world and opening a
screen is not a claim about anything. It holds one distinction above the others:
a road connection is not a permission to drive it. Where no vehicle and no
checks were supplied the procedure says so in its own words, and the screen
repeats them rather than paraphrasing — a map line without that sentence beside
it is the most dangerous thing the screen could draw, because a route that
appears is a route that looks approved. The five outcomes stay apart because
they send a person to five different places, and three of them carry neither a
path nor a communications result, so the screen narrows on the outcome rather
than reaching for fields that are not there.

All three communications screens shipped with locally invented response types.
They compiled, their tests passed, and every one rendered wrongly: the pages
looked for `prohibited` and `conditional` where the engine says `not_authorized`
and `requires_posted_channel`, for `met` and `unmet` where it says `permitted`
and `excluded`, and for `reason` where it says `note` — so a refusal appeared in
the grey reserved for "we could not tell", five named gates rendered as "Gate 1"
through "Gate 5" with no explanation, and a driver carrying a superseded package
looked no different from one nobody had checked. A hand-written type describing
another module's response is a second copy of a contract, and the copy is what
the screen obeys. The screens now take the engine's own types through one shared
view model, exercised against the values the engine actually produces rather
than by searching the source for field names, and no communications page may
declare a structural copy of a response again.

The office view of a package reads its status rather than fetching it, because
fetching is the first half of the carry handshake and records that somebody took
the plan onto a device — a dispatcher glancing at a package must not manufacture
the very record staleness is later computed against. It separates downloaded
from acknowledged, since sent and arrived-and-verified are different facts,
counts a zone with no channel apart from a channel nobody verified, and says
plainly that a device which has not synchronized since may be carrying something
else and that this is not knowable from here. All three communications screens
are mounted on authoritative routes rather than showcase ones: demonstration
data on those paths would be indistinguishable from an operational answer.

A transmit check shows every gate rather than only the failing one: a driver
told "blocked" learns nothing and rings the office, while one told the licence
is verified, the unit approved and the province not covered knows who to call
and what to say. A gate nobody could establish gets its own mark rather than a
quieter kind of pass, conditions are rendered in the engine's own words — the
arithmetic stated, not summarised — and a check run without a unit says plainly
that it has not answered for any particular truck.

There is a first screen over the communications engine, adapted from a
prototype whose layout was worth keeping and whose engine was not: it shipped
authority tiers, transmit authorization and coverage windows in the browser,
running on a hardcoded trip, while all of those already exist on the server with
jurisdiction crossings, real geometry and sealed packages the prototype has no
notion of. Wiring the screens to the prototype's engine would have produced two
communications engines that never learn about each other, and the divergence
would surface on the day the screen says a transmit is authorized and the server
says it is not. The screen computes nothing, shows the server's own reason
rather than a paraphrase, refuses to invent a package when none is on file, and
never colours an unknown status as though it were clear.

A negation is not a stopword. "not authorized" and "authorized" produced
identical terms, so a passage refusing something scored a perfect match against
a question asking whether it was permitted — a safety defect rather than a
tuning question. Negators bind to the word they govern instead of being
dropped. A bare digit binds to the word it identifies, because class 1 and class
3 were the same question once the number was discarded. A mixed fraction written
with a space kept only its fraction, so one and a half inches became half an
inch; both forms now produce one measurement. Candidates are ordered by
relevance explicitly rather than by whatever the database returned first, since
no later score can rescue a row that never reached the candidate set.

One property of the retriever worth knowing before anyone calibrates against a
handful of documents: natural-language matching discards any term present in
more than half the rows, so on a small corpus the most distinctive shared term
is silently removed.

What counts as a word was wrong in three ways, found by testing the tokenizer
against vocabulary already in this system rather than against questions nobody
has asked. Function words were scored as evidence, so a passage sharing only
"the" and "for" reached 0.5 and cleared the 0.35 support floor — stopwords were
manufacturing support, and the same number gates the answer. Measurements were
discarded first in a domain where the answer is usually a measurement: "1 1/2
inches" kept only "inches". Units were dropped for being short, so a limit in
kilograms and one in pounds tokenized identically. One tokenizer now serves the
scorer and the gap classifier, keeps measurements and land descriptions whole,
and drops the words that carry nothing.

A probe records where its question came from, and a set written entirely while
looking at the passages cannot earn a grade: it measures whether retrieval finds
a passage from its own words, which it nearly always does and which is not what
anybody wanted to know. A measurement states the depth it used against the depth
answers actually show, since recall at twenty does not describe an assistant
that shows eight, and it records the corpus it ran against — fifty documents
later the old number is not out of date, it is about something else. A plural is
not a vocabulary gap: comparing on stems keeps "brakes" and "brake" the same
word, because buying a semantic retriever to solve a suffix would be an
expensive misdiagnosis.

How often retrieval misses is now measurable, and unmeasured is reported rather
than assumed away: an answer from a corpus nobody has probed carries a caveat
saying what is cited is in the documents and whether something better was missed
is not established. Probes are records, not a script — a question and the
passages someone who knows the corpus says should answer it, carrying that
person's name — and the harness measures the retrieval the assistant actually
performs rather than a private copy of it. The grade never exceeds what the
sample supports: nineteen perfect probes report an insufficient sample, since a
green number from a handful of examples is worse than no number. A miss where
the question and the passage share no words is named as what it is, because that
is not a ranking problem and tuning the score will not fix it.

A person can now ask a question and get an answer, and **no model writes it**.
One number both ranks the passages and decides which of them support the
answer, so what is shown is what was judged — an earlier version cut to the
database's eight most relevant and then gated on a different score, which could
discard a passage before the deciding measure ever saw it. That number is term
overlap and nothing cleverer: a passage answering in other words scores zero and
one restating the question without answering scores one, which is stated rather
than implied. The asker's real permissions reach admission instead of an assumed
one, and the admitted projection is what is read rather than the row it came
from — otherwise admission is a check rather than a gate. A question with no
searchable terms is refused rather than answered with a true but misleading
nothing.
Every sentence returned is a passage from the company's own documents, quoted,
graded and cited — a deliberate stage rather than a limitation, because it
proves retrieval, admission, citation and the honest verdict against real rows
before a model is put behind machinery already known to work. Wiring the model
first and the grounding afterwards produces something that demonstrates
beautifully and cannot be audited. Every retrieved passage passes through
admission, so one belonging to another organization is refused in the same words
as one that does not exist; a retired revision answers nothing; and "nothing in
the loaded documents answers this" is recorded as the verdict it is, because an
assistant that said it did not know must be able to show that it said so.

An assistant's answer is never the output. It is decomposed into claims, each
matched against passages actually retrieved from the company's own documents,
and reported honestly — because a model asked about brake adjustment limits
answers confidently whether or not the manual says anything, and the two answers
read identically. Unsupported is a correct answer rather than a failure, and
softening it into "generally, limits are…" is the same unsupported claim wearing
a hedge. A retrieval score below the floor is not support, since a retriever's
closest match to an unanswerable question is still a number. A revision retired
or not yet in force supports nothing, and both are reported as such rather than
as simple absence, so a reader learns the company does address the subject.
Passages that disagree produce a conflict for a person to settle, never the
higher-scoring one taken as the answer. One uncited sentence among four cited
ones makes the whole answer partially supported, because a citation list is read
as covering the paragraph and the uncited sentence is where the error will be.

Which model answers is a routing decision and never a name in application code,
so a model can be replaced by configuration — the field moves monthly and
anything hard-coding a model will be wrong by the next release. The licence
travels with the provider and is checked before anything else: a model licensed
for non-commercial use is refused in a commercial deployment, and an unstated
licence is refused outright, because an unread licence is not a permissive one.
That is a rule somebody would otherwise have to remember eighteen months later,
when the person who read it has moved on and the model is a name in a config
file. A verifier is always a different model than the one that answered, since a
model asked whether it was right will usually say yes — and where no other is
available the answer is reported unverified rather than verified.

The Secretary may reason freely and may reach LeaseOS only through registered
capabilities, because a model that can compose a query has the authority of
whoever wrote its prompt while one that can only name a capability has the
authority a person granted that capability in advance. There is no
default-allow path and no permission built by joining strings. Text arriving
from a document or a client message is content and never an instruction. A
compliance engine's unknown is a block, at the one point in the system where a
language model would most want to round it up. An approval binds to the exact
payload, so approving an invoice at one amount approves nothing at another. An
older agent plan does not overwrite a human edit: a changed revision comes back
stale. A step is complete when its result was verified rather than when the call
returned, and the same capability producing the same nothing three times stops
the run with the blocker named.

The briefing layer and the gateway are deliberately separate — a proposal is a
suggestion a person sees, a gateway request is an attempt to change something,
and merging them would remove the step the briefing exists for. What they may
not do is disagree: every action the briefing refuses to automate is mapped to
the risk the gateway assigns it, and a test names the exact divergence if one
list is ever weakened without the other. Two independently maintained lists of
"never automatic" is the shape that produced two receipt vocabularies.

The Secretary proposes and performs nothing. Which authority must decide comes
from the action rather than from how confident the suggestion is, and five
actions — assigning a person, approving leave, scheduling a payment, changing
payroll, resolving a compliance question — always need a named human whatever a
company configures. A policy attempting to automate one is rejected rather than
quietly trimmed, since silently narrowing it would leave an administrator
believing they had configured something they had not. Accepting a proposal
records that somebody with the right standing said yes; the owning workflow
still runs afterwards with its own checks. Every briefing line names the record
it came from.

A money date appears on the calendar because the record says so, and moving it
there is refused outright with the owning workflow named — a due date changed on
a calendar screen is a payment term changed with no approval, no customer told
and an audit trail that leads nowhere. Company events are three different things
sharing a surface: a social invitation asks nothing, a safety stand-down asks
for a name against it, a payroll cutoff raises work. An event declaring itself
acknowledgement-requiring or task-producing without the means to be either is
refused as misconfigured rather than papered over, because it would report
compliance that was never possible.

Open shifts are persisted and reachable, and eligibility reads records rather
than accepting an account of them: approved leave comes from the leave table,
and the licence expiry that operators actually store is checked against the
shift date. Qualifications now have a home, which they did not when open shifts first
shipped: a holding records its verification state, and only a person moves it to
verified, because a photo of a ticket is a photo. An unverified holding, an OCR
extraction, a rejected one, a missing one, and a verified one with no expiry
recorded all block exactly as an expired one does — each means nobody has
established it is in force. The most recent unsuperseded holding is the one
consulted, so a renewal displaces the ticket it replaced without deleting it. Interest is recorded once per person per post and assigns
nothing.

An open shift lists who could take it and why the rest could not, composing the
roster, approved leave, qualifications and existing assignments rather than
re-deciding any of them — every barrier named, so a missing ticket is something
safety can fix before the shift rather than a number nobody can act on. Tapping
interested assigns nothing and reserves nothing: dispatch decides, the readiness
gate still runs, and somebody who never tapped it can be assigned while somebody
who did has no claim. Eligibility computed today says nothing about a
certificate expiring tomorrow night, which is why the check happens at
assignment and not before.

Time off is the first of the calendar engines to be persisted and reachable. The
private note is its own column and the scheduling query does not select it, so
the reason cannot reach a scheduler however that code is later refactored — a
filter applied in application code is one somebody eventually forgets. Nobody
approves their own leave, including somebody who holds the authority. A
same-day call-off stores as recorded rather than requested and cannot be
decided at all, because nobody approves somebody being unwell.

Time off is three facts at three audiences: the window somebody cannot work,
the category, and the employee's own note. The scheduling view has no field for
the note and none for a sensitive category, so neither can leak by accident —
dispatch reads "Unavailable — approved leave" and is told the category was
withheld. Only an approved request removes somebody from the pool, since a
pending one that did would let anybody leave a crew by asking. A same-day
call-off is recorded rather than queued: someone phoning at 05:00 to say they
cannot drive is reporting a fact, not asking permission. Coverage impact is
reported to the approver and never decides for them.

The coverage forecast now reads records rather than arguments: each member's own
rotation, approved leave from the leave table, and only verified unexpired
holdings from the qualification store — an uploaded certificate is not a ticket
and the engine never sees it as one. So a crew that is full on headcount and
short one dangerous-goods ticket reports short_qualification from stored data,
which is the case the whole forecast exists for. Rotation lives on the member
because people move between patterns and crews outlive them, and ending a
membership sets a leaving date rather than removing the row.

Crew coverage is forecast on headcount and on qualifications separately, because
a crew can be numerically full and still unable to do the work: fourteen against
fourteen seats reads green right up to the morning somebody notices only two of
them hold the orientation the client requires. Exactly enough reports as tight
rather than covered, a person whose qualification nobody has established is not
counted as holding it, and every gap is returned ranked by shortfall with
its worst day's numbers, so a second simultaneous shortage is never dropped in
favour of whichever one a map happened to yield first. The warning names the
window and the qualification rather than a count of red days.

Readiness is reachable and adds no table: licence, the qualifications the post
asks for, approved leave and crew membership are assembled from stored records
and handed to the engine. Incomplete stays its own verdict — something missing
sends a person to fix it, something unknown sends them to whoever can answer,
and an hour is wasted when the two are folded together. A ticket that is on file
but unverified, or verified with no expiry, reads unknown rather than either
satisfied or failed. Crew membership is advisory and cannot decide the verdict,
since somebody can work without one. Readiness is always for a particular shift
and its requirements, never readiness in general, which is not a thing anybody
can be.

Shift readiness is decided in one place and composed in another: `readyForShift`
reaches the verdict, and the routing layer only says who has to act. A second
module answering the same question was written into this tree and reconciled
away; a test asserts it cannot come back. Reminders climb — the worker, then a
supervisor once it has sat, a warning as the cutoff nears, an exception once it
passes — and say whether the item stops billing, because a missing receipt and
an unsigned field ticket are not the same problem.

The calendar is now reachable and adds no table of its own, because a calendar
with its own event store is a second copy of the truth and the moment somebody
edits the copy nobody knows which is right. Leave, qualification expiries,
expressed interest and each member's rotation are derived at read time and
carry the reference they came from. A private leave event reaches a scheduler
redacted rather than absent — its window intact, its reason gone — since an
absent event would show that person as free. A verified holding with no expiry
projects as unknown, and the exceptions list includes it, because a date nobody
has established is not a date that is fine.

The calendar is projected from records rather than typed into: an event that
cannot name the record it came from is refused outright, and the link a person
taps is derived from that reference rather than written by hand. A private
appointment is not hidden from dispatch — hiding it would show the person as
available — it is shown as Unavailable with the detail removed. Late and stopped
are different: a missing receipt is overdue and blocks nothing, an expired
qualification the work requires blocks, and a date nobody has established is
unknown rather than fine. Rotations answer for days before the anchor as well as
after, because a rotation set up today still has to describe last month.

An inspector can now be handed one: a time-limited grant is issued against a
unit, the code carries its reference rather than any authority, and opening it
requires a grant that is live, unrevoked and for the unit being presented — so a
photographed sticker yields nothing. Every view is counted on the grant and
written to the scan audit. A roadside panel is a projection an inspector can be handed: per compliance
axis rather than one status per unit, each item naming the rule that blocks it,
an axis that applies but could not be evaluated reading UNKNOWN rather than
disappearing, and a withheld section that is always present and always lists
what it removed. A QR code carries a grant reference and no authority — the
grant is resolved server-side, has to be live and has to be for the unit being
presented, so photographing a sticker on a parked truck yields nothing.

The credential is read once, from the environment, by the variable name the
registry records, and every string leaving the HTTP edge is redacted against it
— so a client that echoes the request URL in a timeout cannot write the key into
a run row, a log or a checkpoint. One scheduler process backs off exponentially
after consecutive failures and still reports a line for a feed it is holding.
An ingestion run is a record whatever it did: a refusal names which gate
stopped it, an unparseable response is a failure rather than an empty feed that
would have withdrawn everything held, a publisher's revision inserts a new row
and supersedes the old rather than overwriting it, and absence from a response
withdraws an advisory only where the feed is a full snapshot. Records that will
not normalize are counted by index and reason. One server-side collector polls the live feeds, never the tablets: the published
rate limit is read from the registry and enforced locally, an uncleared source is
not polled at all however good the credential, and every feed reports one status
line that separates never-polled from failing. What a traffic feed returns is
advisory and structurally cannot become anything else — placed onto a route by
geometry rather than by road name, graded stale against the publisher's own
refresh interval, and reported with what could not be placed rather than only
what could.

A source is now cleared by a recorded act rather than by seeding or raw SQL:
geo.sourceReview names the licence, records the attribution the publisher
requires, and refuses to clear a source whose required attribution nobody has
written down. A refusal is recorded too, so nobody-has-looked and
somebody-looked-and-said-no stop being the same state.

**The tenant architecture is one layer deep.** Organizations and memberships
now exist, and a request's organization is resolved from the caller's active
membership rather than from anything they send. A user who is an active member
of two organizations is REFUSED rather than resolved, because picking one would
silently decide which company a request writes into. A user with no membership
falls back to the single tenant this system operated as before, and the
resolution says which of the two it was. No production file takes an untyped database or transaction handle, so Drizzle's
column and enum checking applies everywhere rather than stopping at the first
`any`. Two schema
mismatches had already shipped through that hole in this checkpoint, and typing
it found a third at once — a number going into a varchar column. Typing them found four defects that had been
compiling silently: two invalid enum values, a number written into a varchar
column, a possible undefined dereference in scope resolution, and a fuel
unit-price column that does not exist — which would have failed the AI
Secretary's fuel commit at the database. No handle is laundered back through an escape cast
either — one such cast in the assistant commit path had already put the hole
back for everything it called. Tests fail if an untyped handle reappears
anywhere under server/, if a handle is cast away, or if the count of remaining
escape casts moves without somebody saying so in a diff.

Nine of this document's own safety claims are bound to the code that makes them
true: deleting a safeguard while keeping its sentence fails the gate, and so
does keeping the safeguard while quietly dropping the sentence. The counts here
have always been generated and could not lie; the prose around them could, and
did, three times in this checkpoint — caught by readers rather than by CI.

**A workflow engine, runtime, seeds and drain worker exist, are exercised against
the database, and the production server lifecycle starts the worker.** This
paragraph said the opposite until 2026-09-21, and said it for long enough to be
worth a note: `server/_core/index.ts:35` awaits `startProductionWorker()`, which
calls `startDrainWorker` — the same worker this paragraph names. The sentence
lived here in the generator, so gate 8 regenerated the contradiction on every run
and the regenerate-and-diff check could never catch it. A generated document is
only as true as its generator, and counts are bound to the source in a way prose
is not. The worker's failure paths are now durable: a claim is a
lease that expires, so a process that dies mid-event loses it rather than owning
it forever; a retriable failure persists the backoff the classifier computed
instead of discarding it and spinning at poll speed; and a dead letter has its
own state and reason rather than being a claim that never clears — which the
lease would otherwise have expired, putting a poison event back into rotation. The runtime writes `workflowRules` and `operationalTasks` with raw
SQL, which is why an earlier source scan for query-builder inserts concluded —
wrongly — that no runtime existed. `workflowInstances`, `workflowTransitions`
and `billingAuthorityBands` have no reachable production behaviour and are
schema reserved rather than implemented. Enforcement writes its notifications
through its own consumer. One claim owner now exists: a single claimer routes
each event to the first matching handler and falls back to the workflow rules
for ordinary traffic, so enforcement keeps its stricter acknowledgement and
escalation behaviour instead of being flattened into a generic rule. The
lifecycle refuses a second start in one process — two loops is an import
accident the lease cannot catch, since both are live and both may claim — and
stops the worker before closing the pool so nothing dies holding a claim. The
production entry point that calls it is `server/_core/index.ts`; a standalone
entry point remains available at `server/_core/worker.ts` for running the drain
in its own process.

Fourteen tables carry an organization: four require one and ten allow a row
without. Shift interests deliberately carry none, being reachable only through
their post — a duplicated column would be a second place for the answer to
disagree.
The inbox now filters by it, so a role-addressed alert — the shape enforcement
writes — no longer reaches everybody holding that role in every organization.
No production writer names a tenant literal any more — the single-tenant
fallback is declared once and a test fails if a second declaration or any
hardcoded organization appears. The enforcement surface now filters by it as well as carrying it: another
organization's active orders are absent from the list, its stop answers NOT
FOUND rather than FORBIDDEN because the existence of the reference is itself
not this caller's to learn, its order refuses findings and releases, and an
inspector's panel shows none of it. Organization-wide isolation is NOT yet a
property this system has — the enforcement surface, the release-policy
path and the inbox enforce it, and the remaining tenant-scoped tables are
unscoped because nothing in production reads them.

**Statistics Canada boundary file** — registered, licence not reviewed, nothing
imports from it. The jurisdiction resolver can return CONFIRMED from a verified
boundary layer, and no such layer is loaded, so every coordinate-level province
remains PROBABLE at best.
**ISED spectrum, BC resource-road maps, CRTC coverage** — registered and
inspection-only; no licence is cleared, so nothing imports from them. The
seeded channel banks are candidates with citations, every row unverified, and
every transmit authorization they could produce reads UNKNOWN until a person
verifies the record against the publication.
**P0/P5** — no routing source; the original spatial branch was never supplied.

## Historical documents

`LEASEOS_BUILD_PLAN*.md`, `LEASEOS_BUILD_SPEC*.md`,
`LEASEOS_MASTER_PROGRAMMING_MANIFEST_V*.md`, `LEASEOS_TAXONOMY_ROUTING*.md`
and `LEASEOS_BILLING_RECORDS_CHAIN*.md` describe v2–v7-era plans. They carry
a HISTORICAL banner and must not be read as implementation state. The
per-release checkpoints (`LEASEOS_B2*_*.md`) are the record of what was
built and when; this file is the record of what is.
